body:
_Migrated from issue #1252, filed 2026-07-30._

`CLAUDE.md` defines safe-tier-1 as "every changed file is a `.po` under `cps/translations/`, or `*.md`, or `README*`. No code." The validator behind `auto-merge.yml` does not check that.

`scripts/lib/tier_policy.py validate-fork-pr --tier safe-tier-1` runs the forbidden-path filename check and the diff-content sensitive-token scan, but no file-type restriction and no LOC cap — those exist only for tier-2. Measured on #1251, which changes three `.md` files plus one `.py`:

```
--tier safe-tier-1 -> {"ok": true, "reason": "", "category": "ok"}
--tier safe-tier-2 -> {"ok": false, "reason": "PR is too large for safe-tier-2 (additions=25, files=4; caps are 80 LOC / 3 files)."}
```

So tier-1 is the *more* permissive label for a PR containing code, which inverts the intent of the tier table. A PR with arbitrary production `.py` changes labeled `safe-tier-1` gets auto-merge enabled on green CI with no size cap and no `CHANGES-vs-upstream.md` requirement (tier-1 is explicitly exempt from that check).

This is not an open door: `tier-label-guard.yml` strips tier labels applied by anyone outside the trusted set, so only we can reach it. The risk is a tick mislabeling in good faith — believing the validator enforces the prose definition, which is a reasonable assumption given tier-2's caps are enforced there. #1251 was merged manually under rule 3 rather than labeled tier-1 for exactly this reason.

Suggested fix: give tier-1 an explicit allowlist check in `tier_policy.py` (`*.po`, `*.pot`, `*.md`, `README*`) that fails validation otherwise, so the label means what the table says it means and the single source of truth actually holds. A test pinning "a `.py` file in the diff fails tier-1 validation" would keep it honest.
title: tier-1 auto-merge validation does not enforce the "no code" clause of its own tier definition
